findings.title: Phone (390×844): every bench camera crops its own controls; in the Arcade only the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins can be tapped, so the clean fixes can't be built by touch
findings.room: arcade, garage, observatory, spectrum (all station benches)
findings.problem: At 390×844 the bench camera uses the same framing as on a 16:10 desktop, so the table runs off both sides of the portrait screen. In the Arcade the left column of block bins (47 Ω and 220 Ω) and the sign-off button on the right are off-screen. I tapped a dense grid over the whole visible bench (every 8 px, x 2–390, y 380–500). Only the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins answered (`phoneTakeable:[100,470]`). Pinball's clean fix needs a 220 Ω block and Rhythm needs 47 ‖ 47, so on a touch-only phone those jobs can't be solved the intended way. The other benches crop the same way. Garage: the 1000 µF cap bin and the left edge of the board are cut off. Observatory: the antenna and cable-route controls on the left and the capacitor can on the right are cut off. Spectrum: the RADIO and MICRO band buttons, the 100 mW power button and SEND are cut off. Only QFN fits. There are no keys to fall back on, because a phone has no number row. This is the NEXT_STEPS open item ('check every bench at 390×844'), and it is still open. The game ships a phone layout (thumbstick, touch action buttons), so this blocks play there.
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/hud-ui-32p-arc-bench.jpg (bins cut at the left edge, sign-off off the right)
src/ui/ui.css:251-258 (phone bench rules move only the cards, never the camera)
findings.fix: Give each station's bench `view` an aspect-aware distance and FOV. When camera.aspect < 1, pull back until the table's world-space bounding box (bins and sign-off button included) fits inside 92% of the screen width: dist = (tableWidth/2) / (tan(fov/2) * aspect) * 1.08. You could also rotate the bench camera to look down the table's long axis in portrait. Put this in a shared helper in src/stations/shared.ts, `fitBench(view, tableBox, aspect)`, and call it from each station's camera update (arcade, garage, observatory, qfn, spectrum station.ts). As a backstop, make the phone bench prompt pill tappable: a tap on it performs its action (see the keyboard-glyph finding).
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/06-controls.mjs: phoneTakeable must be [47,100,220,470]. Retake hud-ui-41p-* for garage, observatory and spectrum: every bin, button and SEND/sign-off control is fully on screen. Add a Playwright spec, 'phone bench fits', at viewport 390×844. For each station, project every clickable's bounding box to the screen and expect it inside [0,390].
findings.verify_reason:
I reproduced this at 390×844 with mockups/review5/tools/verify-hud-ui/01-phone-arcade.mjs. I tapped a grid every 9×8 px over y 360–540, and only the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins answered (phoneTakeable [100,470]). It is worse than the finding says. I built the clean Pinball fix through act(), powered it, and let the soak pass (soakDone:true). The pill then read 'Enter Sign off', but tapping every 10 px over y 300–640 never signed off (signedByTapAt:null). So on a touch-only phone no Arcade order can be completed at all, not just the clean fixes. Shots 41p-garage, 41p-observatory and 41p-spectrum show the same side cropping; QFN fits. One factual correction: the bench camera is not 'the same framing as desktop'. src/game.ts:371-372 already pulls back by distance*clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1). At aspect 0.462, 1.25/aspect is 2.7, so the 2.1 cap is what crops the table. ui.css:251-258 does move only the cards, but the camera is aspect-aware. | P0 re-check confirmed: I couldn't refute it, though there is one undiscoverable workaround. Portrait reproduction at 390×844 (mockups/review5/tools/p0check-hud-ui/01-arcade-phone.mjs, a tap grid every 10 px over x 2–390, y 150–760): only the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins answer (takeable [100,470]). Shot mockups/review5/shots/p0check-hud-ui-01-arc-phone-bench.jpg shows the 47 Ω and 220 Ω bins cut at the left edge. The desktop shot p0check-hud-ui-02-arc-desktop-bench.jpg shows all four bins and the ✓ sign-off button. After building the clean Pinball fix through act() and passing the soak (p0check-hud-ui-06-port-ready.jpg, pill 'Enter Sign off'), the ✓ is only a dark sliver at x≈388. Taps near the right edge (04-signoff-targeted.mjs) hit the power lever and never sign off. So in portrait no Arcade order can be finished by touch.

I found no other touch path. At a bench, a left pointerdown goes only to benchPointer (src/game.ts:172). The bench yaw is forced toward the stand and the distance ignores zoom (src/game.ts:370-372), so the camera can't be orbited or pulled back. The lens option doesn't help either: lensScale(fov, exact=true) keeps the bench framing the same (src/render/lens.ts:11). The prompt pill isn't tappable (src/ui/objectives.ts:93, plain div). Walking/action buttons are hidden at a bench (src/ui/ui.css:246). The station panel is pointer-events:none (ui.css:218).

The workaround is to turn the phone to landscape. At 844×390 (03-arcade-landscape.mjs) all four bins are tappable (takeable [47,100,220,470]). Sign-off works by touch (04-signoff-targeted.mjs: signed at [640,248]), with the ✓ sitting under the pass-through panel (p0check-hud-ui-04-arc-landscape-ready.jpg). Nothing tells the player to rotate, though. There is no orientation hint or lock anywhere in src. The game also designs deliberately for portrait (game.ts:371 portrait pull-back, game.ts:376 portrait title shot, ui.css:251-258 phone bench rules). A portrait phone player is therefore soft-locked at the Arcade bench.

Correction to the verifier's evidence: its sign-off grid (y 300–640, full width) also tapped slots and the power lever. That knocked the built fix off the board, so 'signedByTapAt:null' there was partly an artifact of the test. My targeted run confirms the conclusion anyway. I didn't re-shoot the garage, observatory or spectrum benches; their cropping rests on the earlier 41p shots.

Recommended priority: P0 for portrait. If the team treats landscape as the supported phone orientation, a 'rotate your phone' prompt at benches would cut this to P1. The real fix is still the fit-to-table-width pull-back at src/game.ts:372, replacing the 2.1 cap.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-hud-ui-02p-arc-ready-to-sign.jpg (soak passed, pill 'Enter Sign off', ✓ button off-screen right)
findings.fix_correction: Change the existing pull-back in src/game.ts:372 instead of adding per-station code first. Replace clamp(1.25/cam.aspect,1,2.1) with a fit to each station's table width: horizontal half-FOV = atan(tan(vfov/2)*aspect), dist = max(v.distance, (tableHalfWidth*1.08)/tan(hHalfFov)). An optional `width` on each station's `view` gives the table width, so no station needs its own camera code. At about 2.8× pull-back the monitor text gets very small on a phone, so also consider a portrait-only bench layout (bins and sign-off moved under the board). The pill-tap backstop only helps single-key prompts (see finding 11).

findings.title: No gamepad control reaches any bench: 5 of the 9 jobs can't be played on a pad, even though the HUD shows pad glyphs
findings.room: all station rooms (arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum)
findings.problem: Game.pollPad maps only A jump, X grab, B cable, Y throw, Start pause, Back camera and L3 survey (src/game.ts:187-190). At a bench, X calls interact(), and interact() calls leaveBench() (src/game.ts:200). Station input comes only from keyboard codes passed to station.key() (src/game.ts:164) or from mouse ray picks. Nothing maps a pad to pick, slot, flip, power or sign-off. With a gamepad connected, the HUD switches to pad glyphs (`hud gp`, hud-ui-60d) and promises full support. Yet a pad player who sits at the Arcade bench can only stand up again. Every station job (Arcade, Arcade Rush, Garage, QFN, Observatory, Spectrum) is unfinishable on a pad. That breaks DR-22 (controls consistent across rooms) and DR-25 (no job left unfinishable).
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/07-gamepad.mjs (emulated pad: X grabs the plug and B drops it, so the pad is live)
findings.fix: Add a bench focus cursor for pads. In each station, expose an ordered `clickables` list (they already exist for mouse picking) plus a `focus(i)` method. In Game.pollPad, when atBench: the d-pad or left stick moves focus to the nearest clickable in that direction, A calls station.act(focused.act, focused.arg), B leaves the bench (instead of X), Y is the station's main verb (power, pulse or send), and Start pauses. Draw the focused clickable at 1.08× scale with the existing hover highlight. Show the pad glyph in the bench pill (A Take a 47 Ω block).
findings.verify: New spec tests/gamepad.spec.ts. Stub navigator.getGamepads as in mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/07-gamepad.mjs, then play Arcade cabinet 1 with pad buttons only and expect snapshot().station.served.length===1.
findings.verify_reason: Code: Game.pollPad maps only {0 jump, 2 grab, 1 cable, 3 throw, 9 pause, 8 camera, 10 survey} (src/game.ts:190). Both grab and cable call interact(), and interact() leaves the bench when atBench (src/game.ts:197, not :200). I reproduced it with mockups/review5/tools/verify-hud-ui/02-arcade-keys-pad.mjs and an emulated pad seated at the Arcade bench. A made Pip jump while seated (y 1.36, then 2.01 after Y), Y did nothing, B (not only X) stood Pip up, and the d-pad, LB, RB and RT did nothing. X sat him back down. No pad input ever changed held, setup or powered. The HUD is in 'gp' mode. The count is wrong: the station jobs are arcade, arcade-rush, garage, qfn, observatory and spectrum, which is 6 of the 9 jobs, not 5. Priority: a desktop browser with a gamepad always has a mouse and keyboard, which still finish every bench. So this is a broken secondary input path rather than a job no player can finish; P1, not P0.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-hud-ui/02-arcade-keys-pad.mjs output padButtons: A y 1.36 atBench true; B atBench false; X atBench true; setup and held never change
findings.fix_correction: Same plan, with two notes. B already leaves the bench via action('cable'), so keep B as stand-up and stop X (grab) from leaving. Also stop A from jumping while atBench (gate it in Game.action or in pollPad).

findings.title: R restarts instantly with no confirm, also at the bench: one stray key next to E/F wipes a run
findings.room: all rooms (worst in meeting, lunch and station benches)
findings.problem: KeyR calls action('restart'), which calls location.reload() immediately while playing (src/game.ts:166, :178). R sits between E and T, right next to the two core keys E and F. In the Meeting, holding the power strip, one press of R reloaded the job with no prompt (2.2 s to ready). At the Arcade bench R isn't a station key, so it falls through to the same handler and the bench run is lost (`RreloadsAtBench:true`). The Observatory teaches R as 'reroute the cable' at its bench (src/stations/observatory/station.ts:306), so a player who has learned that will hit R in the Arcade, Garage or Spectrum and lose everything. This breaks DR-19 and DR-22 (a key never destroys progress while the player is trying something, and the same key means the same thing everywhere). Retry itself is quick (2.2 s, DR-20 passes); the problem is that it happens without the player meaning it.
findings.fix: Make R a hold-to-restart during play: hold R for 0.8 s, with a radial fill on the pause button. A tap does nothing in play, so only the pause menu's Restart tile and the result/fail cards restart on a tap. At a bench, swallow KeyR unless the station maps it: return true from Game's bench branch for any unmapped letter key, src/game.ts:164. Rename the Observatory 'route' key to one no other bench uses, or keep R and make it bench-local everywhere.
findings.verify: Extend mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/06-controls.mjs: a tap of R in the Meeting while holding the strip gives no navigation and held stays 'strip'; holding R for 0.9 s reloads. At the Arcade bench a tap of R gives no navigation.
findings.verify_reason: Code: KeyR in play calls action('restart'), which calls location.reload() (src/game.ts:166, :178). GameUI.key flags autostart first (src/ui/game-ui.ts:119), so the reload drops straight back into a new run. At the Arcade bench the station has no KeyR, so the key falls through. I reproduced it: RreloadsAtBench:true in verify-hud-ui/02-arcade-keys-pad.mjs. It is worse than reported: R is bench-local at two benches, not one. Observatory maps KeyR to 'route' (src/stations/observatory/station.ts:305-306) and QFN maps KeyR to 'rotate' (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27). A player who learned R there and presses it at the Arcade, Garage or Spectrum bench wipes the run.

findings.title: Arcade bench prompt 'P Fuse cooling' invites a key that switches the bench OFF (DR-19 still open)
findings.problem: After the PTC fuse trips, the key pill reads 'P Fuse cooling'. That is a status, but it is shown as a key action. Pressing P, as the pill suggests, toggles the bench power off. After the player fixes the chain and presses P, the snapshot reads powered:false, live:false. Once the fuse has cooled, the bench sits dead and the pill changes to 'P Power on'. So the player has to press P twice, and the first press, made exactly as told, undid their retry. DR-19 names this case directly ('power, then trip, then fix the chain, then P. The run should end with live===true, not POWER OFF').
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/08-arcade-p.mjs result: trip {powered:true,tripped:true,pill:'P Fuse cooling'} → afterP {powered:false,live:false,pill:'P Power on'}
findings.fix: In src/stations/arcade/station.ts: (a) while tripped, prompt() returns a pill with no key, or with the hover hint, never 'P …'. (b) act('power') while tripped && powered is a no-op that plays the cooling tick (or it stays powered and auto-retries when cool), and never sets powered=false. The fuse self-resets, so the bench comes back live once it cools.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/08-arcade-p.mjs: afterP must be {powered:true,live:true}. Add the same sequence to tests/station-arcade.spec.ts.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced with verify-hud-ui/02-arcade-keys-pad.mjs. After the trip the snapshot read {powered:true,tripped:true,pill:'P Fuse cooling'}. After the fix the pill still read 'P Fuse cooling'. Pressing P gave powered:false, and 6 s later {powered:false,live:false,tripped:false,pill:'P Power on'}. Code: prompt() returns {key:'P',text:'Fuse cooling'} while tripped (src/stations/arcade/station.ts:486), and act('power') calls powerOff() whenever powered (:268-269). This is exactly the DR-19 check case. The pill shows a status, the 'Fuse cooling' row is also on the panel, and the monitor shows 'FUSE COOLING 2.0 s' (hud-ui-33d), so this one fact appears three times.

findings.title: Touch players can't orbit, zoom or survey: the camera is right-drag, wheel and Tab only
findings.problem: Orbit starts only on pointer button 2 (src/game.ts:172), zoom only on the wheel event (src/game.ts:175), and survey only on Tab or pad L3 (src/game.ts:166, :190). A touch pointer is button 0, and a tap on the canvas goes to action('grab') (src/game.ts:172). The phone action bar offers grab, cable, throw, jump and camera reset (src/ui/screens.ts:50-55), with no survey or zoom button and no two-finger orbit. A phone player is stuck with the default yaw and can't swing the camera around a wall or cabinet that hides Pip (DR-12). They also can't open the survey the rules require on a phone (DR-21), and zoom doesn't work in every room (DR-22). The phone survey I forced through Tab also shows only the middle third of the lobby (hud-ui-04p).
evidence: src/game.ts:172 (orbit only on e.button===2; tap = grab)
src/ui/screens.ts:50-55 (touch action bar has no survey or zoom)
findings.fix: In setupInput: track active pointers. One-finger drag on empty canvas (not on the stick) orbits, using the same yaw/pitch factors as right-drag. A tap under 200 ms with less than 8 px of travel still grabs. Two-finger pinch changes zoom (clamped 9..38). Add a small survey button next to the camera button in the touch bar (`act small survey`, icon 'survey' already exists in src/render/icons.ts). For portrait, make the survey zoom fit the room: zoom = max(44, roomDepth/(2*tan(fov/2)*aspect))*1.05.
findings.verify: Playwright with hasTouch:true at 390×844. Touchscreen drag over the canvas changes yaw; pinch changes zoom; the survey button toggles snapshot survey. Retake hud-ui-04p: every lobby door is visible.
findings.verify_reason: Code: orbit starts only on e.button===2, and a button-0 pointer (every touch) calls action('grab') (src/game.ts:172). Zoom is wheel-only (:175). Survey is Tab or pad L3 only (:166, :190). There are no touch or pinch handlers anywhere in src (grep for touch/pointerType/coarse finds only a comment). The phone action bar in hud-ui-03p and hud-ui-04p has camera reset, throw, plug, jump and grab, but no survey or zoom. hud-ui-04p (survey forced with Tab) shows only the middle of the lobby, which fails DR-21 in portrait. I did not run a hasTouch drag, but the code path is unambiguous.
findings.fix_correction: Same plan. Note that the thumbstick already captures its own pointer (src/ui/game-ui.ts:136), so a canvas one-finger drag won't clash with it. Keep the tap-to-grab threshold so grab still works.

findings.title: Gamepad mapping disagrees with its labels: 'RS' is shown for camera reset, but RS-click does nothing and Back resets; L3 survey is never shown
findings.problem: The action bar's camera button and the pause controls map both pair the reset-camera icon with an 'RS' pill (src/ui/screens.ts:55, :169). In code, reset is button 8 (Back/View) and survey is button 10 (L3) (src/game.ts:190). Button 11 (RS click) is unmapped. With an emulated pad, pressing RS after an orbit changed nothing (mean pixel diff 2.4, which is noise), while Back snapped the camera home (diff 76). Survey on L3 appears nowhere on the title, the pause map or the HUD. Sprint isn't listed for the pad either. Also, with a pad connected, the prompt pill still prints keyboard keys ('F Pick up the plug') while the action bar shows B (hud-ui-60d).
evidence: mockups/review5/shots/hud-ui-60d-pad-hud.jpg (pill says F while the bar says B)
findings.fix: Either map 11 (RS click) to 'camera' and keep the RS label, or change the label to the View/Back glyph. Add the survey row to the pause controls map (Tab / L3) and to the title controls strip. In ObjectivesHUD.update (src/ui/objectives.ts:116), when the layer has class 'gp', translate prompt keys through a table {E:'X',F:'B',Q:'Y',Space:'A',Tab:'L3',Esc:'B'} and render them with the btnpad colour classes.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/hud-ui/07-gamepad.mjs: the RS press now resets the camera (large diff). The pill in hud-ui-60d shows a red B glyph. The pause screen shows a survey row.
findings.verify_reason: Code: pad reset is on button 8 and survey on button 10. Button 11 (RS click) is unmapped (src/game.ts:190), yet the action bar and the pause map print 'RS' for the camera (src/ui/screens.ts:55, :169). I measured the reviewer's shots: mean grey difference hud-ui-61d vs 62d (after RS) = 2.4, i.e. no change; 62d vs 63d (after Back) = 76.0, i.e. the camera reset. The verify-hud-ui-03 pause text has no survey row. hud-ui-60d shows the pill 'F Pick up the plug' while the bar shows a red B, because ObjectivesHUD prints p.key raw (src/ui/objectives.ts:121).

findings.title: Workshop picker is mouse/touch only and doesn't take over input: Tab can't focus it, a pad can't pick or close it, and E/WASD/Start still act behind it
findings.problem: The picker opens over a live game (src/hub/lobby.ts:108-117). It doesn't pause, take focus or swallow keys. Tab is preventDefault-ed as survey (src/game.ts:166), so three presses of Tab left document.activeElement on BODY, and Enter did nothing. A keyboard-only player can't choose a practice job. On an emulated pad, X opened the picker. Then B, A, Y and the d-pad did nothing to it, and Start opened Pause on top of it (hud-ui-65d). A pad player can't pick or close it. Movement keys still drive Pip while it is open: advance with KeyW moved Pip 1.26 m with the picker up (01-menus.mjs pickerkeys). The prompt pill 'E Workshop: practise any station', the job card and the action bar all stay live behind it. Re-check of L3: the scrim and the phone fit are fixed and the titles are left-aligned, but the HUD stays live and the spelling is still mixed. This breaks DR-22 ('No game key acts while a menu is open').
findings.fix: Treat the picker as a modal screen. Set game.paused-like input gating (a `modal` flag checked at the top of Game's keydown and pollPad), focus the first button on open, and let arrow keys or the d-pad move focus and Enter or A activate. Esc, B or E close it, and number keys 3–7 pick directly (they match the printed job numbers). Hide .prompt-pill and .actions while it is open (body[data-modal] rule in ui.css).
findings.verify: Lobby spec: open the picker, press ArrowRight then Enter, and expect the URL to match /level=garage&practice/. With an emulated pad, pressing B closes it. With the picker open, holding W for 1 s leaves the player position unchanged.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced with verify-hud-ui/03-overlaps-picker.mjs. With the picker open, holding S for 0.8 s moved Pip 3.36 m and the picker stayed open. Three presses of Tab left focus on BODY. ArrowRight then Enter left the URL unchanged. E did not close the picker (it reopens via hub.interact → openPicker). Only Esc closes it, through the capture listener in src/hub/lobby.ts:115. Code at lobby.ts:108-117 adds no modal gating or focus. The pad half (X opens it; B, A and Y do nothing to it; Start pauses over it) matches Game.pollPad, which has no picker branch.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-hud-ui/03-overlaps-picker.mjs output: pickerMove 3.36, pickerFocus 'BODY.', pickerAfterE true, pickerAfterEsc {open:false}

findings.title: Bench text load is 45–73 words, and the same values appear on the job card, the side panel and the bench monitor (DR-40/DR-41 still open)
findings.room: arcade, garage, observatory, qfn, spectrum, arcade-rush
findings.problem: I measured the visible words in the card, panel, toast, pill and chip at 1440×900 bench views: Arcade at trip 69, Arcade passed 59, Observatory 71, QFN 73, Spectrum 62, Garage 45. The rulebook cap is about 25 outside the monitor. The duplication is systematic. Arcade: 'Red LED on 5 V: 12–20 mA' is on both the card and the panel, and Chain 220 Ω, Current 13.6 mA and Hottest block 41 mW are each on both the panel and the monitor. Observatory: 'Clean up the garbled message' is on both the card and the panel, and Signal/noise 4.0 dB is on both the panel and the monitor's 'S/N 4.0 dB'. Spectrum: 'Visible 530 nm', 'no signal' and 'Pod not on the pad' each appear on both the monitor and the panel. Garage: 'Resets on shutdown' is on the card and the panel, and the panel's 'Across motor/switch/controller —' rows repeat labels printed on the board. Arcade Rush: the countdown is in the jobplate clock (2:59) and again in the panel ('RUSH · 179 s'). The trip toast alone is a 20-word sentence. On phone the panel collapses to the ask, which proves the extra rows aren't needed to play.
findings.fix:
At the bench, hide the job card (it already hides on phone, ui.css:252; do the same on desktop) or reduce it to dots only. Drop every `.build` row whose value the monitor already draws: Arcade chain/current/hottest; Observatory S/N, tone and latch; Spectrum band, link and pod; Garage slot rows. Keep only the parts-cost credit and anything not on the monitor. Remove the story `

` once the first action is taken, or fade it after 4 s (DR-40). Cut fault toasts to one clause, for example 'Block across the LED: no limit, fuse tripped'. Target 25 words or fewer at every bench.
findings.verify: Re-run 04-arcade-bench.mjs and 05-benches.mjs: `words` ≤ 25 in every bench state. Retake hud-ui-33d/41d-* and confirm that no number appears twice on screen.
findings.verify_reason: I checked hud-ui-33d and hud-ui-34d. In 34d the values 220 Ω, 13.6 mA and 41 mW are each on both the monitor and the panel, and 13.6 mA appears twice on the monitor alone (CURRENT and the LIGHT row). 'Red LED on 5 V: 12–20 mA' is on the card and the panel. In 33d 'fuse cooling' is on the panel, the monitor ('FUSE COOLING 2.0 s') and the pill. My own word count of 33d (card, panel with story, toast, pill, chip) is about 65–70 words, far over DR-40's ~25. The panel markup is at src/stations/arcade/station.ts:449-451 (not 444-449), and the RUSH countdown is built there too (`RUSH · N s`).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/hud-ui-34d-arc-bench-pass.jpg (220 Ω / 13.6 mA / 41 mW on the monitor and the panel)

findings.title: Job card and key prompt disagree at the start of Meeting (known) and of Lunch (new)
findings.problem: In the Meeting start shot the card reads 'Fetch the power strip by the printer and set it at the boardroom door' while the pill reads 'F Pick up the plug'. This is known DR-42, re-checked and still open. Lunch has the same problem. The card reads 'Wedge the kitchen door open with the doorstop' while the pill reads 'F Pick up the thin cable end', and walking toward the reels gives 'F Pick up the thick cable end' while the card still says wedge. At the Spectrum desk the card's current step is 'Carry the receiver pod into the brick storeroom', yet the room offered 'E Work at the desk' first, and at the desk the pill reads 'E Fetch the pod', where E only stands Pip up. promptFor() takes the nearest affordance (src/ui/objectives.ts:69-90) with no knowledge of the current step. A new player follows the bright pill and the card becomes noise. The two text elements AGENTS 2 allows contradict each other on the first screen.
findings.fix: Pass the current step to promptFor, using a `wants` tag on each Step, e.g. {wants:['strip']} or {wants:['wedge']}. If the nearest affordance isn't in the current step's wants and isn't critical, show it in a quieter pill style (no yellow kbd, 60% opacity), or show nothing. Spawn Meeting and Lunch Pip a few metres from the reels (Meeting spawn toward the printer; Lunch spawn by the corridor door), so the first prompt is the first step. For Spectrum, don't offer 'Work at the desk' while step 1 (carry the pod) is open, or reorder the steps.
findings.verify: Retake hud-ui-20d, hud-ui-22d and hud-ui-41d-spectrum: the pill names the card's object or is hidden. Add an objectives.spec.ts assertion at t=0.5 s per level: the pill text contains the step noun or is empty.
findings.verify_reason: verify-hud-ui/03-overlaps-picker.mjs at t=1 s. Meeting card: 'Fetch the power strip by the printer and set it at the boardroom door', pill 'F Pick up the plug'. Lunch (desktop and phone) card: 'Wedge the kitchen door open with the doorstop', pill 'F Pick up the thin cable end'. promptFor checks lunch.promptAt and nearest affordances with no knowledge of the current step (src/ui/objectives.ts:65-85). findings.title: Bench pills on phone print keyboard keys (1–4, P, Enter, 1–3) that a touch player can't press
findings.problem: At 390×844 the bench pill shows '1–4 Take a block', 'P Fuse cooling', 'Enter Sign off', 'P Pulse the motor', '1–3 Take a can' and 'E Fetch the pod'. A phone has no such keys and the pill isn't tappable (pointer-events:none, src/ui/ui.css:208). Touch players get instructions they can't follow, and the hover hint that names the bin ('1 Take a 47 Ω block') never fires on touch, because there is no hover. AGENTS 2 allows a one-line key prompt; on a phone that line has to describe a touch action.
findings.fix: When matchMedia('(pointer:coarse)') is true, render the pill's kbd as a tap glyph (the existing 'hand' icon) and use verb-only text ('Tap a bin', 'Tap the lever', 'Tap ✓ to sign off'). Make the pill clickable at a bench (pointer-events:auto), so a tap runs the prompt's action through station.act. Implement this in ObjectivesHUD.update, src/ui/objectives.ts:116-117.
findings.verify: Retake hud-ui-32p, hud-ui-33p and hud-ui-41p-*: no digit or letter keycap on coarse-pointer devices. Playwright with hasTouch: tapping the 'Sign off' pill signs off.
findings.verify_reason: Phone bench shots show keyboard-only pills: 1–4 (hud-ui-32p), 'Enter Sign off' (verify-hud-ui-02p), 'P Pulse the motor' (41p garage), '1–3 Take a can' (41p observatory) and 'E Fetch the pod' (41p spectrum). .prompt-pill has pointer-events:none (src/ui/ui.css:208). Hover hints fire only on pointermove, which a tap doesn't produce, so the bin-specific hint never shows on touch. QFN's 'Drag Draw from a pad' (41p-qfn) shows that a touch-worded pill is possible.
findings.fix_correction: Making the pill tappable only works for single-action prompts. Prompt has no action field, so add an optional `code` to Prompt (e.g. 'Enter', 'KeyP') and call station.key(code) on tap. Multi-key prompts like '1–4' or 'A S D' can't map to one tap and still need the bench to fit on screen (finding 0).

findings.title: Bonus stars on the job card are unexplained during play, and two light up at t=0
findings.problem: The card ends with three tiny stars (about 9 px at 1440×900) that track bonus goals. The code comment says 'their wording is on the pause and result screens' (src/ui/objectives.ts:108-109), but the pause screen has no bonus text. The pause markup is header, tallies, buttons and controls map only (src/ui/screens.ts:150-172, and the pause innerText in 02-playground.mjs). The stars are 'currently satisfied' rather than 'earned', so 'Finish in under 45 s' and 'Break nothing' are gold the moment the Playground starts (hud-ui-10d) and then go grey. findings.fix: Add the bonus list (icon, short text, ok state) to pauseMarkup and fill it in GameUI.paused() from objectives.results(). Draw keep-type bonuses (time and no-damage) as outlined 'at risk' stars until the job ends, and fill only achievement bonuses (pins down) as they happen. Raise the star size to 16 px.
findings.verify: Retake hud-ui-14d: pause shows three bonus rows. hud-ui-10d: no filled star at t=1 s except an achieved one.
findings.verify_reason: hud-ui-60d shows two gold stars at 0:00 in the Playground. Bonuses are computed live each frame (src/ui/objectives.ts:105, :115). The pause text in my lobby run is 'HQ | Circuit Crew Hq | 0:03 | … | RS', with no bonus wording, and hud-ui-14d also shows none. Bonus text appears only on the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts:217). findings.title: Objective marker is a small unoutlined pale cone, about 15 px at the lobby and garage cameras, and it melts into the doors (DR-44)
findings.problem: The marker is a fixed 0.42 m world-size cone with outlines turned off (src/ui/objectives.ts:97-98), placed at y≈2.1 m. At the lobby home zoom (23) it measures about 15 px tall and sits over the Cable Playground door's window, pale yellow on teal and cream, with no outline or shading. findings.fix: Scale the marker by camera distance each frame (marker.scale.setScalar(max(1, camDist/14))) so it stays at least 28 px. Turn its outline on (remove outlineParameters visible:false) or add an ink back-face shell at 1.12× scale. Make it 2-tone (lit top #ffd84a, shade #e0a92a) and set depthTest:false with renderOrder 10, so it draws over clutter and walls. For doors, raise the anchor to y=2.9 so it sits above the door frame. Change the lobby card text to 'Go to 00 · Cable Playground'.

findings.title: Bench key handling leaks game verbs: Space jumps Pip out of the chair, C resets the orbit at QFN while also 'checking', Tab silently toggles survey, and E means 'stand up' while the pill says 'E Fetch the pod'
findings.problem: Game's keydown bench branch (src/game.ts:164) passes any code the station doesn't map on to the normal handlers. In one Arcade bench session: Space made Pip jump to y 1.59 while seated (afterSpace), and Tab flipped game.survey even though the bench camera hides it, so the next stand-up opens straight into survey. GameUI also runs KeyC → camera reset with no bench check (src/ui/game-ui.ts:127), so QFN's 'C check' (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27) resets the orbit too. Letters also change meaning per bench: F is flip at Arcade and Garage but plug elsewhere; S is slot 2 at Arcade but series at Observatory; R is route at Observatory but full restart elsewhere; P is power at Arcade and Spectrum but pulse at Garage. E is both 'leave bench' and the advertised verb in 'E Fetch the pod' (Spectrum), where pressing it only stands up. DR-22.
findings.fix: In the bench branch, after station.key(), swallow every remaining key except Esc/E (stand up) and P-for-pause equivalents: `e.preventDefault();return;`. Guard KeyC in GameUI with !game.atBench. Publish one bench key grammar for all stations: 1–5 parts, A/S/D places, Space primary action (power/pulse/send), Enter sign off/log/ship, Backspace undo, F flip, and a per-station letter only for a unique control. Change Spectrum's at-desk prompt to 'Esc Stand up to fetch the pod'.
findings.verify: Bench key-matrix script: Space, Tab, C and Q at each bench leave player.y, survey and camera yaw unchanged. The Spectrum pill no longer says 'E Fetch the pod'.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced with verify-hud-ui/02. Space at the Arcade bench gave y 1.59 while atBench stayed true. After Tab at the bench, standing up opened straight into the survey (verify-hud-ui-04d). Code: the bench branch falls through for unmapped codes (src/game.ts:164), and GameUI's KeyC has no bench check (src/ui/game-ui.ts:127), so QFN's KeyC 'check' (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27) also runs action('camera'). At the bench the yaw is forced each frame (game.ts:372), so the visible effect only appears after standing. Extra: on a pad, A jumps while seated. The Spectrum 'E Fetch the pod' part is weaker than stated, because standing up is the first step of fetching the pod. It is still a status written as a verb.
extra_evidence: verify-hud-ui/02 kSpace {atBench:true,y:1.59}; pad A y 1.36 at bench

findings.title: Pause menu lacks the controls a player needs mid-job (Tab survey, Shift sprint, Esc stand up) and offers no assists (DR-23)
findings.problem: The pause controls map lists move, grab, plug, throw, jump and the camera only (src/ui/screens.ts:162-170). Survey (Tab), sprint (Shift) and stand-up (Esc at a bench) aren't listed. The 'Sound' tile is drawn in the selected/green style while the others are paper, so it reads as the selected option rather than a toggle state. notes.clarity: What works well: the HUD vocabulary is coherent. The ink-outlined paper cards, the yellow kbd pill, duotone icons, the striped-cable motif shared by the title, Jobs and result screens, and the dots-plus-current-step job card all read as one system. In the cable rooms the start frame text is small: Playground is about 9 words (card plus pill), and the pill matches the card there. The result card shows clearly which axis earned the grade (the highlighted row with the cable feed into the stamp). Benches use diegetic labels well: A/S/D printed under the Arcade sockets, PULSE/TEST plaques in the Garage, ROUTE: PAST MOTOR in the Observatory. The problems are density and duplication at the benches (45–73 words, with the same values on the card, panel and monitor), card/pill disagreement at the Meeting and Lunch starts, key glyphs that don't match the input device (keyboard letters on phone and pad), and a few small polish issues (the HQ icon clash, 'Hq', practise/practice, unexplained bonus stars). The marker reads in the Playground but not at the lobby or garage distance.
notes.playability: Desktop keyboard+mouse play is solid in the cable rooms: E/F/Q/Space/Tab work as labelled, Esc pauses, Esc at a bench stands up, retry is about 2.2 s and lands straight in play (DR-20 passes), and Tab/R are gated to play (L6 fixed). The serious gaps are input coverage. (1) On phone, every bench except QFN crops its bins and buttons off-screen; in the Arcade only the 100/470 Ω bins can be tapped, so the clean fixes can't be built. Touch also has no orbit, zoom or survey. (2) On a gamepad, no station job can be played at all: bench input is keyboard and mouse only. The RS label is wrong, and the Workshop picker can't be closed or used. (3) R is an instant, unconfirmed reload that also fires at most benches, right next to E/F. (4) The Arcade 'P Fuse cooling' pill makes the player switch the bench off. Smaller leaks: Space jumps Pip out of the bench chair, C resets the orbit during QFN checks, and the picker leaves the game live behind it.
notes.fun: From the HUD side, the juice is good. The plug-in hitstop and flash, the strain bar shifting white→red with the pill flipping to 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' at strain >0.97, the win push-in keeping Pip in frame on desktop, the result rows counting up with a stamp thud, and the Lunch fail tag that swings in with steam all land well. Things that undercut the fun: bonus stars that start lit and then go out, a bench screen that feels like a spreadsheet (59–73 words), and losing a run to a stray R. On phone the result and fail cards cover the whole frame, so the win push-in is never seen there.
notes.teaching: The HUD supports teaching mostly through the bench monitors and the board labels, which are good. The HUD side panel repeats what the monitor already shows instead of adding to it, which works against Mayer's redundancy principle (DR-41). The Lunch fail card shows the result (spoiled food, a hot thermometer) but not the cause, so a player who missed the fridge doesn't learn that it needed power. The Arcade toasts are full-sentence explanations ('The block across the LED limits nothing: the LED still sits straight across 5 V, so the fuse tripped.'). They are accurate, but they are a 20-word read laid over the work. Shortening them to one clause, and moving the 'why' onto the monitor, would keep the play-by-doing balance.
notes.models: Not my dimension. HUD icons (src/render/icons.ts) are on a consistent 32-unit grid with ink strokes and read well at 28–40 px. The damage (cracked mug) and cost (coins) tally icons are legible without labels. The marker cone is the one 3D HUD element, and it lacks the ink outline every other model has.
